title: fix(browser): avoid standalone routing errors and cropped screenshots

commit.messageHeadline: fix(browser): avoid standalone routing errors and cropped screenshots
fix(protocol): retain named schema types in declarations
chore: merge main and retain upstream protocol fix
chore: merge main into browser repair
fix(browser): bound interrupted captures and release stale metrics
fix(browser): distinguish embedded contexts from Gateway owners

Codex review: found issues before merge. _Reviewed September 1, 2026, 8:47 PM ET / September 2, 2026, 00:47 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes The PR routes unpinned standalone browser calls to the local host, preserves screenshot geometry through Playwright page ownership, and serializes interrupted screenshot, resize, and device-emulation operations. ## Regression provenance Possible regression — suspected (reviewed change). No predecessor PR is attributed. ## Merge readiness ⚠️ **Ready for maintainer review - 4 items remain** Keep open: the prior P1 compatibility finding remains on the exact current head. An existing standalone setup with only a local Gateway port is now forced to the host browser instead of performing its former node discovery, despite the added `mode="auto"` guidance requiring an upgrade-time configuration change. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `2fc9fa3b14d78369ceeeaf719864b93a662f212a` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | The screenshot and interruption work has substantial test coverage, but the unresolved P1 default-routing regression prevents a merge-ready rating. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: Not applicable under the stated MEMBER authorship; the PR body nevertheless supplies claimed real Chromium geometry and recovery evidence. The remaining blocker is the source-proven routing upgrade regression, not missing contributor proof. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: Not applicable under the stated MEMBER authorship; the PR body nevertheless supplies claimed real Chromium geometry and recovery evidence. The remaining blocker is the source-proven routing upgrade regression, not missing contributor proof. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 6 items | Introduced compatibility change: The introduced condition returns the host route when no explicit node policy exists and the caller is standalone, including a configuration that only supplies a local Gateway port.
Current-main baseline: Current main unconditionally called node discovery after the existing manual/off and explicit-target checks; it did not classify a local-port-only standalone configuration as host-only.
Regression test encodes the changed behavior: The added standalone-routing table explicitly expects a local-port-only configuration to use the host and not call node discovery, so it does not preserve the former upgrade behavior. | | **Findings** | 1 actionable finding | [P1] Preserve standalone node routing for local Gateway upgrades | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The browser plugin selects a host, sandbox, or Gateway/node browser target before issuing page actions. Screenshot, resize, and device changes then share per-page Playwright/CDP state that determines rendered geometry and recovery after interruption. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Standalone agent] --> B[Browser route selection] C[Gateway and node settings] --> B B --> D[Host browser or browser node] D --> E[Page-owned CDP and Playwright state] E --> F[Screenshot resize and device actions] F --> G[Agent-visible result or recovery error] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should standalone configurations with only a local Gateway port preserve their existing automatic browser-node discovery, or should host-first routing become an intentional upgrade policy? | **Preserve local Gateway discovery:** Keep node discovery for the existing local-Gateway configuration and use host routing only when no Gateway route is selected. | Why: The branch changes a default route for existing configurations, and the new opt-in `mode="auto"` instruction does not establish that operators accept the resulting behavior change. ## Before merge - [ ] **Preserve standalone node routing for local Gateway upgrades (P1)** - A standalone configuration with only `gateway.port` previously reached `listNodes`, but this introduced branch now returns the host route before discovery. Users with a reachable browser node and no usable host browser can fail or control a different browser; the new `mode="auto"` documentation is an upgrade-time configuration change, not compatibility preservation. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Merging changes the default for existing standalone configurations that specify only a local Gateway port: a reachable browser node may be bypassed in favor of an unavailable or different host browser. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The bug-fix branch has a production net increase of 66 lines; it is partly offset by removing the former viewport-restoration path, but the added public routing fact and queue lifecycle should be accepted only with the routing policy decision. ## Findings - [P1] Preserve standalone node routing for local Gateway upgrades — `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.routing.ts:53-58`

Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, from source: run an unpinned standalone browser action with only a local Gateway port and an available browser node; current main calls node discovery, while this branch returns the host route first. The review worker did not execute it because the read-only environment could not start Corepack. Is this the best way to solve the issue? No: the screenshot and interruption repair is coherent, but the routing change is not the best complete fix until it preserves existing local-Gateway discovery or maintainers explicitly approve the upgrade behavior. Users with a reachable browser node and no usable host browser can fail or control a different browser; the new `mode="auto"` documentation is an upgrade-time configuration change, not compatibility preservation. The routing upgrade decision is to keep local browser control for unpinned standalone runs. This is the intended behavior of this maintainer repair. `gateway.port` is inherited listener/derived-port metadata, not node selection. The v2026.8.2 discovery behavior does change: standalone workflows that rely on a local Gateway's implicit browser-node discovery should use the existing `gateway.nodes.browser.mode="auto"` or an explicit node target/pin. The PR body and browser docs make that path explicit.

The focused proof also found a missing distinction in the real command path: `withLocalGatewayRequestScope` creates an embedded RPC context, and the initial predicate incorrectly counted it as a running Gateway. The final correction records that fact at the context producer. Caller/ambient real Gateway bindings remain authoritative after retirement, and local RPC stays available.

Before the correction, the actual local admission owner plus public Browser tool failed with `GatewayCredentialsRequiredError`. Afterward, the same port-only configuration completed two real host status calls without discovery. Explicit `auto` retained real auth errors and, with a connected-node transport fixture, selected and invoked `browser.proxy` under the same local scope. The real local-context regression was red before repair; all 23 local-context/RPC checks now pass. The successful node result uses a transport fixture; no remote node or model was involved.

The earlier screenshot-timeout finding and both rank-up moves remain addressed by native Chromium stall/recovery proof. The final signed head is `4b4566ee4322aa014713230aa86d259f19e267db`; exact-head CI is running.

Merged via squash.
